posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
I guess to explain what I mean by "easy" villains, I tend to look at the ratings as

1. Any team can beat them with relatively little trouble, and losses are attributed to extreme bad luck or spectactular failure to prepare. These are starter villains you use to introduce the game to people.

2. Any team can beat them, there'll be some trouble, but for the most part, playing straightforwardly will get the job done.

3. Any team can beat them, but you'll have a lot of trouble if you don't know what you're in for and you're much more likely to lose to carelessness.

4. Any team can beat them, provided they draw the right cards quickly and the villain draws its least useful cards until you've had several rounds to set up. Winning reliably all but requires not only that you know what you're in for, but that you have a team specifically suited to the villain and are lucky.

"Well, you have to wipe your board now or die" and "Well, you have to wipe your board now and you die" are the kinds of out-of-nowhere kicks in the head that feel out of place on villains supposed to be rated at the lowest difficulty. I expect Dawn to have something like that. But with Dawn, you can avoid it if you're prepared.

I've had Wraith go from nearly full health to completely wiped out because of one Technological Singularity that came out despite diligent Infrared Eye-Piece use. To my knowledge, it's the only card that can pop out so unexpectedly and outright kill you because you've gotten set-up fully, and there's no way to mitigate the effects once the card pops up (unlike Devious Disruption, which lets you destroy stuff first).

It's like the boss in the video game's tutorial level randomly one-shotting everyone. It just feels wrong to me that the two lowest-rated villains are the ones I make sure to have deck control for, but against higher rated villains like Voss or Gloomweaver I feel I can usually leave it behind.

It's not that I think the villain should be easy because there's an "arbitrary difficulty number attached." It's that the game says that they're the lowest difficulty villains. I mean, presumably they didn't assign those numbers randomly – the number is there to represent a given value of difficulty.

That said, take away Devious Disruption and Technological Singularity, and Blade and Omnitron are really easy. Omnitron's most dangerous cards take effect at the start of his turn. The drones' effects multiply if there's more out, but Omnitron can at most play two drones around, and you have to be trying to not have a party that can manage at least four damage a round. The only way he's threatening with the drones is if there's a really rough Terraforming that puts out several all at once (which is still preferable, to me, to putting out Technological Singularity)

Blade's damage is either minimal or focused on the highest HP hero. Impending Doom becomes his most dangerous card because it plays another card, but even that's not so bad except for how often it seems to lead to Devious Disruption.

So it's not that I think they should be easy – it's that those cards feel really out of place compared to the rest of the deck they're in.

(Fun little side note: It's interesting that most of the hardest villains are built in a way that deck maipulation does relatively to them. The Chairman is always shuffling his deck, The Matriarch doesn't really care which bird is on the top of her deck, because she's going to play eight more regardless, and picking which of two or three ways Iron Legacy is going to kill you is time better spent getting your affairs in order before Iron Legacy kills you.)

I'll have to disagree on the Chairman – you can at least keep him from putting two Underbosses out at once. The Matriarch, yeah, unless you're lucky you're just gonna get two birds, but things like Suggestion are still useful.

Also disagree on Iron Legacy – you can at least limit who he's hitting and keep him from putting out another buffing Ongoing.

posts.cooked:
I respectfully disagree with these definitions of the difficulty levels.

I don't think level 1 villains are meant to be easy tutorial villains that you discard after inevitable victory.

I think they are meant to be villain easy to understand both in the way they play, and the way you can beat them. They are the villain that teach you the strategies you will use later in more complex fights, like the value of sacrifice - or the fact that a good set-up is not necessary to do something.

Blade with his countdown is a good example, I think : to beat him, you have to learn to hit hard and fast, even if it means not losing time trying to prevent the damage he does. Even if it means having AZ use all is one-shots without taking the time to put a module in play. It's one of the reasons I rarely use him as the first Villain to teach new players, by the way. Another being that nearly all the cards in his deck are frighteningly powerful - his only weakness being that he rarely does anything more than playing one of them and politely ending his turn…

The fact that they have devastating cards  is what makes them still interesting to play for an experienced player, in my opinion. Yes, they are a tutorial - but not a tutorial on how to play the game, like in a video game. They are a tutorial about how to think when playing SotM.

The higher the villain difficulty level, the harder it is to juggle all the seemingly less devastating effects they have.

I have probably something like a thousand games under my belt now - and I still play against Blade, Omnitron, Ambuscade and friends - because they still have ways to surprise me and push me in a corner where I have to improvize and use everything I know to win, even if it's only in one game from time to time.

About Devastating Aura : it may be a frustrating card. But even with it, Dawn is less difficult to fight than the Organization. The card feels devastating - but is just a temporary setback, not an instant lose.

Maybe the fact that I rarely play non-random teams taints my apreciations of the villains and what I expect a fight to be in SotM.

Don't nerf my Villains  !
